1.point: Open with a hook and state that the chapter will show why knowing ourselves is the way to knowing our Lord, and how.
steps: A familiar prayer line confesses neglect of the soul
The soul was given into our care and deserves it because all knowing happens through it
The soul also knows itself directly, with nothing in between
Knowing God directly would have to happen in the same place, so the chapter begins with the soul

2.point: The Qur'an makes the outcome of a human life depend on what is done with the soul: purify it and succeed, betray it and fail.
steps: Surah al-Shams swears by the soul and the discernment God placed in it
Its next verses make success and failure turn on purifying or betraying the soul
So the human story is the soul's story

3.point: Knowing God starts with knowing the soul, because forgetting one means forgetting the other and knowing one means knowing the other.
steps: Forgetting God causes forgetting the soul (al-Hashr)
So remembering God brings the soul back into view
Losing the soul loses faith (al-An'am): a seen soul shows its Maker
The link runs both ways, as the saying 'whoever knows himself knows his Lord' states
It holds because the soul reflects its Maker
Therefore knowing God begins with knowing the soul

4.point: God is already present to the soul; what separates us is a veil over the soul, and the seeker should lift it in this life rather than wait for death to do it.
steps: We are already in God's presence; what we lack is perception of Him
So the journey to God is the removal of veils over the heart, not travel
Every soul will have the veils removed at the promised meeting with God, where it sees its own soul
What a soul perceives then depends on what it perceives now
So the seeker begins lifting the veils in this life

¶1.label: advance
¶1.why: The hook: a familiar prayer line that is a confession, introducing the quotation.

¶2.label: advance
¶2.why: Reads the confession as being about the soul: given into our care, and neglectable. First link from hook to the soul.

¶3.label: advance
¶3.why: Supplies why the soul deserves care: everything we know, we know with it.

¶4.label: advance
¶4.why: Adds the step that the soul knows itself directly (knowledge by presence); ¶5 relies on it to say direct knowledge of God must happen in the soul. Dense for an opening, but used.

¶5.label: advance
¶5.why: Draws the conclusion (irfan begins with the soul) and states what the chapter will establish, as the point asks.

¶6.label: advance
¶6.why: Introduces Surah al-Shams, the oath by the soul and the gift of discernment, and sets up the verses the point rests on.

¶7.label: restate
¶7.why: Paraphrases the displayed verse in two sentences that say the same thing; the verse already supplies this step and ¶8 draws the conclusion from it directly.

¶8.label: advance
¶8.why: States the section's conclusion (the human story is the soul's story) and closes the loop with the Munajat's confession, which Section 3 picks up.

¶9.label: advance
¶9.why: Links the previous point to the new one and introduces al-Hashr: forgetting God is the cause of losing the soul.

¶10.label: aside
¶10.why: Sheikh Bahmanpour's estimate that most of us have forgotten our souls, and the reassurance about punishment, are not used by any later step; the chain runs from ¶9 to ¶11 without it.

¶11.label: advance
¶11.why: Supplies the first direction: remembering God returns attention to the soul. The stages sentence is extra, but the step is needed.

¶12.label: advance
¶12.why: Supplies the second direction, soul to faith, and introduces the al-An'am verse.

¶13.label: support
¶13.why: Explains why losing the soul loses faith: a soul that is seen shows its Maker. ¶14 and ¶15 build on this.

¶14.label: advance
¶14.why: Puts the two directions together (forgetting is mutual, so knowing is mutual) and introduces the saying the point rests on.

¶15.label: advance
¶15.why: Gives the ground of the saying: the soul reflects its Maker. Partly overlaps ¶13, and the 'not part of God' caveat is a guard rather than a step.

¶16.label: advance
¶16.why: States the conclusion once and backs it with Tabataba'i's 'window of his own soul'.

¶17.label: advance
¶17.why: First step: we are already in God's presence; what is missing is perception.

¶18.label: advance
¶18.why: Draws the consequence: the journey is veil removal, not distance; defines hijab and qurb.

¶19.label: advance
¶19.why: Brings in the meeting with God at which veils are lifted for everyone, and introduces the verse.

¶20.label: advance
¶20.why: Reads the verse: every soul meets God by having its layers removed and seeing itself as it is. Overlaps ¶19 on 'every soul' but adds that the meeting is seeing the uncovered soul.

¶21.label: support
¶21.why: Reconciles 'seeing the soul' with the verse's 'meeting with Him' via the soul-as-reflection idea from ¶15. The believer/unbeliever sentence is a side remark; the main claim is largely ¶20 again.

¶22.label: aside
¶22.why: The limit on encompassing God, with Imam Khomeini's qualification, is true but nothing later uses it; deleting it leaves ¶23 and the conclusion intact.

¶23.label: advance
¶23.why: The step the 'in this life' part of the point depends on: what is perceived then depends on what is perceived now.

¶24.label: advance
¶24.why: Draws the conclusion (begin lifting veils now) and adds a second reason; the sentence on methods aiming at veil removal ties back to ¶18.

¶25.label: aside
¶25.why: Maliki Tabrizi describing what the seeker finds is a second authority repeating what ¶18, ¶20 and ¶16 have established; ¶26 does not depend on it.

¶26.label: restate
¶26.why: Summarises the section (God near, soul reflects Him, veil lies over the soul) after ¶24 has already stated the conclusion.

¶27.label: aside
¶27.why: A bridging question to the next chapter; it supplies no step toward this section's point.
